page-display.purpose: The start page's one h1, "Sing the first line. / The words appear."; balanced wrapping; the vh term keeps the button above the fold.

page-headline.purpose: The example's heading on the start page, centred.

page-lede.purpose: The one sentence under the start page's h1, Soft Charcoal, max 30em, balanced.

display.purpose: The sung lines, Charcoal, 400, left-aligned; sized per bhajan to the largest that fits between the slide's rules (18px to 110px), one sung line per row.

headline.purpose: The bhajan's name and pitch "(ladies / gents)", bold and centred over a 2px Rule Grey rule.

meaning.purpose: The English meaning in italics, Soft Charcoal, over the slide's closing 2px rule.

body.purpose: One-sentence status under the listen button, Soft Charcoal; also the search field.

label.purpose: Choice pills, panel rows and search results. Search pill 15px / 500; wordmark 19px / 700 / -0.02em.

note.purpose: Caption hint, panel notes, figure captions, search lines, in Quiet Charcoal; footer 13px. Inline lyric cues use 0.5em of the lyric size at 500.

key.purpose: Keycap letters; 12px in Soft Charcoal inside the search pill.

shortcut.purpose: Shortcut labels beside their keycaps on the start page, 15px Soft Charcoal; hidden on touch screens.

shadows.name: button-lift
shadows.purpose: The round listen button; removed when disabled.

shadows.name: glass-float
shadows.purpose: Volunteer panel and search sheet, with backdrop-filter: blur(30px) saturate(1.3).

shadows.name: screen-lift
shadows.purpose: The start page's preview screen only.

shadows.name: bar-edge
shadows.purpose: The top bar once scrolled, over rgba(253, 248, 232, 0.92) with backdrop-filter: blur(20px) saturate(1.4).

shadows.name: ring-outline
shadows.purpose: Listening rings over a transparent background; inset 0 0 0 2px #5c5c5c once singing is heard. Never filled.

motion.name: glide
motion.purpose: iOS-like, no overshoot. Things that move: button glides and dock, hover/press, panel and sheet pop, the start page settling away.

motion.name: arrive
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out. Things that appear: page headline and lede, cycle, title, lyric lines, meaning, rings, fills, caption, download arc, the slide leaving.

motion.name: button-handoff
motion.value: inline -> lifting (2 frames, no transition) -> floating (0.95s glide) ... landing (0.95s glide to the slot) -> inline
motion.purpose: The one listen button leaves the start page's slot for the fixed layer and returns to it; focus follows.

motion.name: dock
motion.purpose: Button glides to bottom centre after the first lines start arriving.

motion.name: page-clear
motion.purpose: The start page clears when listening starts; returns with opacity 0.45s.

motion.name: page-enter
motion.value: h1 rise 1.05s arrive at 0, lede at 0.12s, cycle fade 1s at 0.3s

motion.name: lyric-rise
motion.value: 1.05s arrive; title at 0ms, first line 260ms, 90ms stagger, meaning 120ms after the last line
motion.purpose: Each element rises 0.4em and sharpens from a 14px blur, once.

motion.name: slide-leave
motion.purpose: The whole slide fades and blurs 10px.

motion.name: download-arc
motion.purpose: The progress ring around the waiting button.

motion.name: ripple
motion.value: 3s arrive, 3 rings 1s apart, from 90% opacity to 1.85x, in a layer at 70% that fades over 0.5s
motion.purpose: Listening; gone by 70% of the cycle. Never restarted: the layer fades in and out.

motion.name: hearing
motion.value: ring layer to 100%, rings to Quiet Charcoal over 0.6s; bars scaleY 1 to 0.45, 0.9s alternate
motion.purpose: Singing heard; same ring rhythm. Bars ease back to rest over 0.4s when it stops.

motion.name: pop
motion.purpose: Volunteer panel and search sheet open.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: No glides, page scale, rings or bars; one static ring at 50% and 1.35x; headline, lede, title, lyrics and meaning fade over 0.5s; the slide leaves with a plain fade.

slide.rule: 2px solid #9e9e9e, under the title and under the meaning, full slide width
slide.lyricsFit: bisection to the largest size that fits; max min(20% stage height, 7.5% stage width, 110px); min 18px; wrap below 40px (26px under 640px stage width); the preview never wraps
slide.preview: container units inside a 16:10 screen (1:1 below 640px): inset 6cqh 6cqw; title clamp(12px, 3.4cqw, 44px); meaning clamp(9px, 1.5cqw, 19px)

page.hero: min-height calc(100svh - 64px); statement, 132px button slot, 64px caption space, cycle (max 980px) over a 2px rule, More cue
page.dividers: 2px Rule Grey opens a group; 1px hairline rgba(51, 51, 51, 0.12) between rows

narrative.northStar: The Centre's Slide, in the Centre's Colours
narrative.overview:
Bhajan Cue puts up the slide the Sai centre already projects, from a reference slide the user shared: a warm cream page, the bhajan's name and pitch bold and centred over a rule, the romanised lyrics left-aligned below in regular weight, and the English meaning in italics over a closing rule. The room already knows how to read this layout. Since October 2026, by the user's request, the app wears the Sai organisation's own colours rather than the slide's greys: the cream ground stays, the type is a navy ink drawn from the brand blue, titles are brand blue, and saffron (the colour of Swami's robe and of the emblem's centre) carries the listen button, the slide's rules and the listening rings. The Sri Sathya Sai Global Council, U.S.A. emblem (the general emblem, never the 100th birthday one) sits in the top bar and closes the start page, and a photo of Swami, framed in an arch as on a centre's altar, opens it. Around that the app keeps Apple-style restraint: one round button, Shazam-style rings, lines that rise out of a blur, and motion that glides and never bounces.

There are two densities. The start page says what the app does in as few words as possible and then shows it: a sticky bar with the emblem, wordmark and search; Swami's photo; his words as the headline, "Any devotional song, in any language can be sung as long as all can follow." (Sai Bhajana Mala, 29, chosen by the user), credited "— Sri Sathya Sai Baba", and one sentence saying what the app does; and the listen button with its caption. On scroll, a real bhajan set in a screen under "What the hall sees", a single line of keyboard shortcuts, the emblem and the source. The moment listening starts, the page clears and the screen holds only what the room needs this second: the button and its rings, then the slide with the button docked small beneath it. Everything the volunteer might need beyond that (home, search, other matches, what was heard, full screen) sits in quiet shaded circles in the bottom-right corner. The slide's scale is set for a projector read from the back of a hall by an audience that skews older.

The system is light only (`color-scheme: light`, theme colour cream). Navy ink on cream holds about 13.6:1 and the blue title 7.6:1, so the words stay strong on a washed-out projector.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream page; navy ink; brand-blue titles; saffron button, rules and rings; ray orange only around Swami's photo.
The Sri Sathya Sai Global Council, U.S.A. emblem in the top bar and footer, never recoloured or captioned.
Swami's photo on the start page, one of six, a different one each visit, in an arched frame.
The slide: bold centred title with pitch over a rule, left-aligned regular-weight lyrics, italic meaning over a closing rule.
Lyrics sized to fill the space between the rules, one sung line per row.
One solid saffron object: the round listen button.
One system type stack (SF Pro on Apple devices); page headlines are 700 and tightly tracked, the sung words are 400.
The button is one object that sits in the page, lifts out, glides to the middle, docks under the slide and lands back.
Glide and exponential ease-out motion; nothing overshoots, nothing moves while people sing.
rules: **The Sai Palette Rule.** Cream, navy ink, brand blue, saffron and ray orange; nothing else. No gradients, no glows, no tinted bands.
**The One Solid Rule.** The round listen button is the only solid saffron object. Everything else is type, a rule, a hairline, a 7% shade, cream glass or the photo.
**The Saffron Is Not Text Rule.** Saffron and ray orange draw the button, rules, rings and the photo frame. Words are navy or brand blue.

**The Emblem Rule.** The emblem is the Sri Sathya Sai Global Council, U.S.A. general emblem (`src/assets/emblem.png`, from the user's 2000px transparent PNG). Never the 100th or 99th birthday logos, never recoloured, cropped or placed on a busy background, and never captioned with its own name or values. At least 44px tall.

**The Page Voice Rule.** Start-page statements are 700 with tight tracking (-0.025em to -0.03em) and balanced wrapping. The slide never borrows that tracking: its title is -0.01em and its lyrics -0.005em.

**The Say It Once Rule.** The start page says what the app does once, in as few words as possible (the headline and one sentence, by the user's request), and then shows it (the example slide). No step-by-step explainer, no feature blurbs, no repeated call to action; anything the button's caption or the slide already says is not said again.

**The One Line, One Row Rule.** Every sung line sits on a single row so singers see where a line ends. Wrapping is a last resort: only when the one-row fit would fall below 40px (26px on stages under 640px wide) do long lines wrap, at line-height 1.1 with a 0.5em gap between sung lines. The start page's example never wraps.

**The Largest That Fits Rule.** Lyric size is never a fixed step on a scale; it is the largest size at which the whole bhajan fits between the title rule and the meaning. Only outliers that overflow even at 18px with wrapping scroll, inside the stage, fading out at the bottom edge.
**The Slide Weights Rule.** On the slide the title is 700, the sung words 400, the meaning 400 italic in Soft Navy. The lyrics are never bold.
**The Button Keeps The Middle Rule.** On the start page's first screen the listen button sits near the middle, under the statement; nothing above it may push it below the fold.

**The Nothing Else Rule.** Once listening starts, and in the found state, the screen shows only the button (and its rings), the slide (title, rule, words, meaning, rule) and the corner circles. No header bar, no list, no progress bar. The start page is the only place with a bar, sections or explanation.
**The Slide Order Rule.** Title and pitch, rule, lyrics, meaning, rule: always in that order, always inside the slide's margins. The lyrics take whatever height the title and meaning leave.
**The No Boxes Rule.** The start page has no cards, boxes or tinted bands. Two objects are framed: Swami's photo, in its arch as on an altar, and the preview screen, because it depicts a screen.
**The Lifted Few Rule.** Only the listen button, Swami's photo, the glass sheets and the preview screen cast shadows. The slide, every rule, pills and corner circles are flat.
**The Outline Ring Rule.** Listening rings, the download ring and the progress ring are strokes only, never filled discs.

**The Honest Progress Rule.** The progress ring follows the session's real clock and checks. A segment never completes before its check has run, the ring never closes without an answer, and it never names a candidate before one is shown.
**The One Button Rule.** There is one listen button, and it travels: page slot, centre, dock, and back. It is never duplicated: the start page has no second listen control.

**The Words First Rule.** When a bhajan is found, the progress ring closes first (0.66s, so the answer reads as the end of the wait, by the user's request); then the button leaves the middle at once while the title rises and the first lyric line follows at 260ms. The room's eye goes to the words, not to the control.

**The No Snap Rule.** Nothing on the button starts or stops mid-motion. The rings run at one steady rhythm inside a layer that fades in and out; hearing fades them out, never changes their timing; the bars start from rest and ease back to it. A snapping button reads as jitter.
**The Still While Singing Rule.** Motion happens only at the change from one bhajan to the next. Once the meaning has arrived, nothing on screen moves.
